 :JUDGMENT:
The Petitioners in M.V.C. No.5021/2022 and MVC.5020/2022 have filed the Petitions against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
each for the injuries sustained by them in a Road Traffic accident.
2.
Since both these Petitions arises out of the same accident, these two cases were clubbed together and taken for common disposal.

3. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 10.02.2021 at about 9.40 p.m. the Petitioner in MVC 5021/2022 being rider and petitioner in MVC 5020/2022 being a pillion rider of Motor cycle Bajaj Discovery bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-HR-9753 were proceeding on NH.48 road near Mahimaprua Gate, the rider of the said vehicle was riding the same very carefully and cautiously on the said road, at that time, the driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. No.KA-52-T- 2721 and KA-52-T-2722 drover the same at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, took sudden left turn without any indicators and indications and the said Motor cycle dashed against the Tractor from behind.
Due to the tremendous impact, the petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner in MVC.5021/2022 was shifted to Swasthya Hospital, Nelamangala wherein he was treated as an inpatient and later shifted to NIMHANS and from there shifted to K.C. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner in MVC.5020/2022 was shifted to Swasthya Hospital, Nelamangala wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.
She spent nearly of Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and nourishment expenses..

4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.No.5021/2022 was hale and healthy and he was working as a Worker/Helper in a private firm and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
5.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner in MVC.5020/2022 was hale and healthy and she was a House maid and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

6. The Petitioners of both the Petitions have contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. No.KA-52-T-2721 and KA-52-T-2722 which is owned by the Respondent No.2 and insured with Respondent No.1.
As such both the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
7. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents in both petitions, Respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed its detailed Objection Statement.
The Respondent No.2 did not appear before the court and hence he was placed Exparte.
8. In both the petitions, Respondent No.1 has denied the age, avocation and the income of the Petitioners.
Further it denied that the accident has caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in both the petitions and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioners.
Further it admits the issuance of insurance in respect of Tractor-Trailer bearing No.KA-52-T-2721/2722.

It contended that the driver of offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and the owner of the said vehicle knowingly and willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who had no valid driving licence.
Hence, there was breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it contended that owner of the insured Tractor-Trailer has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It is further contended that at the time of alleged accident, the rider of Motor cycle drove the same in high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the rear portion of the Tractor-Trailer,
hence, the rider of the Motor cycle is solely responsible for the accident.
Further it contended that at the time of alleged accident, the pillion rider was not wearing safety headgear.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss both the petitions.

REASONS 15. Issue No.1 in MVC No.5021/2022 and MVC No.5020/2022:-It is the case of the Petitioners that they sustained injuries in the accident caused by the driver of the offending Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. No.KA-52-T-2721 and KA-52-T-2722.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. In order to prove the case of the petitioners, Petitioners in both the cases have been examined as P.W.1 and PW.2.
They got marked 16 documents as per Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-16.
Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-6 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot Panchanama along with sketch, Wound certificate, IMV report and Charge Sheet.

17. Upon going through the said documents, Ex.P.1 and 2 are the true copy of FIR and Complaint which show that the case was registered against the driver of the Tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-52-T-2721 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex .P-3 is the Spot Panchanama along with sketch which show that the concerned police had drawn the Spot Panchanama and prepared sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
As per the sketch the accident occurred on middle of the road which is the National High way.
Panchanama further shows that the driver of the offending Tractor while proceeding on the main road in front of the bike of the petitioners took his tractor left without any indicator.
Hence, the petitioner had hit behind the Tractor.
These documents prove the nature of accident as narrated by the petitioner.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner in MVC.5021/2022, it shows that he sustained grievous as well as simple injuries.
Ex.P-5 is IMV Report, wherein the Motor Vehicle Inspector has opined that the accident was not taken due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.
It further shows that no damages found on the Tractor-Trailer and the bike was damaged.
Obviously, when a bike hit the tractor, the chances of damages to the Tractor is very less as it is heavy vehicle.

Ex.P- 6 is the True copy of Charge-sheet, it shows that the driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-T-2721 and KA- 52-T-2722 was charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC.
18. Ex.P-7 is the Out-patient record, which shows that the Petitioner in MVC.5021/2022 had taken treatment as an outpatient at K.C. General Hospital, Bengaluru.

Ex.P-8 and 12 are the X-rays,
Ex.P.9 is the Medical Bills, Ex.P.10 is the Medical prescriptions, Ex.P.11 is the notarized copy of aadhar card of PW.1.
19.
Ex.P.13 is the notarized copy of Aadhar card of PW.2, Ex.P.14 is OPD card of petitioner in MVC.5020/2022, Ex.P.15 is the Medical bills and Ex.P.16 is the Medical prescriptions.

Ex .P.22

MLC Register Extract show that the history of injury was mentioned as RTA on 10.2.2021 at 9.40 a.m.
21.
There is no dispute about the nature of accident and involvement of the vehicles in the accident.
The Respondent No.1 in its written statement contended that the driver of the tractor had no valid and effective driving licence.
Wherein it has not taken contention about implication of driver in the charge sheet.

But in the cross examination of PW.1 and 2, learned counsel for Respondent No.1 suggested that the accused shown in the charge sheet was not the driver of the offending vehicle, but one Suresh was the driver of the offending vehicle.
Since the Suresh had no driving licence, one Rajanna T.V was falsely implicated.
In this regard, all the suggestions posed by the learned counsel for Respondent No.1 have been specifically denied by the PW.1 and 2.
Nothing worth is elicited to prove the alleged contention of the Respondent No.1.
In order to prove the contention of the Respondent No.1, it has examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and its internal investigating official as RW.2.
They have reiterated the said contention in their examination in chief and they have relied upon the investigating report which conducted by RW.2 and a CD marked at Ex.R.1 and 3.

According to the Respondent No1 the alleged report and the CD about the statement of the public who have seen the accident and the accused shown in the charge sheet have informed the RW.2 that the accused shown in charges sheet was not driving the Tractor at the time of accident, and one Suresh was driving the Tractor.

It is pertinent to note here that during the course of cross-examination of RW.2, in the presence of both counsels, at the request of learned counsel for petitioner, this court had tried to play the CD which is marked as Ex.R.3 but, it was not played.
Therefore, the said CD would not helps the case of the Respondents.
In the cross-examination of RW.1 he admits that the accused shown in the charge sheet had informed the RW.2 that he was not driving the tractor at the time of accident.
But, for the reasons best known to the Respondent No.1 it has not made any efforts to examine the accused shown in the charge sheet to prove their contention.
Further, Rw.2 clearly admits that in Ex.R.1 report no mention that when, where and whose presence he had met the accused and recorded the statement of the accused.
Further, he clearly admits that he does not know whether the information found in the CD might have been tampered one.
Under such circumstances, the Respondent No.1 has failed to prove its alleged contention that the driver of the tractor was falsely implicated.

22. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the depositions and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tractor-Trailer and in the said accident, the Petitioners had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.

23. Issue No.2 in MVC No.5021/2022 :- As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. No.KA-52-T-2721 and KA-52-T-2722 by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 32 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhar card at Ex.P.11 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 16.04.1988.
The accident took place on 10.02.2021.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 33 years to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
25. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was working as Worker/Helper in a private firm and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not lead any evidence to prove the income.

Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, this Court is of the opinion that,
notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2021 notional income of Rs.15,000/- p.m. is taken for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
26. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
27.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex. P.4
Wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.

1. Avulsed laceration present over front of right knee measuring 10cm x 8cm x bone deep with degloving of overlying skin 2. Laceration present over the right lateral malleolus measuring 10cm x8cm x bone deep.
3. Laceration present over the right forehead measuring 2cm x 1cm x0.5 cm.
4. Laceration present over the left upper measuring 3cm x1cm x bone deep 5.
Tenderness present over the left upper chest region.
Wherein, the Doctor has opined that the injury No.1, 3 to 5 are grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
28.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injury sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:

sentences.text: The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence and the documents produced by the Petitioner shows that he had sustained grievous injuries.
As per the discharge summary found in Ex.P.20-Case sheet, Petitioner was treated as an inpatient from 10.02.2021 to 11.02.2021.

Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 2 days.
30.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under this head (@ Rs.15,000/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
31.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
32. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 35 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.9 which is totally amounting to Rs.1,53,579/-.
I have gone through the medical bills.
They found correct.
Moreover there is no dispute about the said medical bills.
Hence, the bills are accepted.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,53,600/-. as a compensation under this head.

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
33.

The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is not able to lead a normal life prior to the said accident.
He unable to do his work and suffered loss of income due to accident.
But in order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce evidence.
However, he has not examined any doctor to prove his disability.

34. Moreover, the PW.1 in his cross-examination, para 9, he admitted that he was attending the Court on the date of his cross-examination by obtaining leave and he took salary of Rs.28,000/- on last month.
If this admission is taken into consideration, it is clear that the result of accident has no impact on the earning of the petitioner from his avocation.
This factor also justifies that as a result of accident PW.1 has not sustained any financial loss.

47. Regarding Liability :

As already discussed above, Petitioners have proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.
No.KA-52-T-2721 and KA-52-T-2722.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 insurer and Respondent No.2 owner are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
